aiOverview.content: The historic Artemis II mission successfully launched from Kennedy Space Center's Launch Pad 39B on April 1, 2026, at 6:35 p.m. ET, carrying four astronauts on a 10-day mission around the moon. This first crewed lunar flyby since 1972 marks a major milestone for human spaceflight. Upcoming launches can be tracked via the official visitor complex schedule. official visitor complex schedule Key Details for Upcoming Launches Location: Launches typically occur at Kennedy Space Center (KSC) or Cape Canaveral Space Force Station (CCSFS). Viewing Areas: The Kennedy Space Center Visitor Complex offers dedicated, ticketed viewing areas with live commentary. Kennedy Space Center Visitor Complex Public Viewing: Free viewing is often available at beaches and parks along the Space Coast, such as Titusville, Cocoa Beach, and Jetty Park, though visibility depends on weather and launch trajectory. Watch Online: Official launches are streamed on the NASA YouTube Channel. NASA YouTube Channel Upcoming MissionsFollowing the Artemis II launch, upcoming schedules include commercial cargo missions to the International Space Station, potential SpaceX Starlink launches, and further development of the Artemis program, which aims to send humans back to the moon. Launch Complexes Launch Pad 39A: Primarily used for SpaceX Crew Dragon and Falcon Heavy launches. Launch Pad 39B: Used for NASA's Space Launch System (SLS) and Artemis missions. Cape Canaveral SLC-40/SLC-41: Frequently used for Falcon 9 and Atlas V rockets. Watching TipsLaunch schedules are subject to change due to weather or technical issues. It is highly recommended to check for "scrub policies" and monitor social media for real-time updates on launch day. scrub policies
